data.body:
Plan rewritten after verifying every claim in the original description against the tree (commit 960fbfef2f).

Claims found FALSE and removed:
- `build_usage_limits` returning the bare `req_limit` was described as a drift bug. It is deliberate and documented at structured_run.py:427-432 (RP-01 S2): telemetry and `completion_banking.iteration_limit_for`'s 2*B inverse both read the bare base; the output-retry allowance is an addend only inside the constructed UsageLimits. Making it allowance-inclusive would BREAK both readers. The old AC `iteration_limit_for(build_usage_limits(...))` was also not type-correct — build_usage_limits returns a 3-tuple.
- `completion_recovery.py:307`, `passes.py:388` and `fidelity_spot_eval.py:103,115` were listed as single-turn sites. All four are `execution_mode="agentic"`. `passes.py:520` is single_turn but `mode="text"`, so it is not part of the structured construct either.
- `code_review/workflow_ops.py:604` — the RunRequest is at :612.
- `workflow/interpreter.py` was in the guard allowlist as a direct RunRequest site; it constructs `BatchRunRequest`, a different class.
- The site list omitted two real single-turn structured sites: `evals/eval_solver.py:167` and `plan_review/__init__.py:172`.
- AC1 asked that judge_one and judge_batch declare the same bound set. `kaolinite-head-wildebeest` (3939) closed exactly that as not_a_bug: judge_one has no production caller. Bounding it is out of scope now; it gets an explicit `bounds=RunRequest.INHERIT_POLICY` (behaviour unchanged).
- A required `model_class` argument was dropped: several adopting sites deliberately inherit `cfg.model`, so forcing a class would change which model they call — a behaviour change, and bug afeb's mechanism already owns that question.
- `iteration_limit` dropped from the builder: a single_turn run has `tools=[]` and `req_limit = max(1, ...)`, so it is a no-op there.

Claim found TRUE and kept: only judge_batch declares the four lowering-only seams, and only completion_recovery.py:413 sets a token cap — verified by grep over src/rebar.

New scope item the original plan missed: `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py::_run_request_sites` matches only `node.func.id == "RunRequest"`. Adopting a classmethod makes fourteen sites invisible to it, so the oracle would FAIL OPEN while its frozen 24-entry table assertion fails. The fix is three lines in the matcher; the table's keys, config expressions and verdicts are untouched.

Line accounting: the original plan implied net-negative. Honest estimate is about line-neutral — the description says so rather than claiming otherwise.
